title: Annotatio I §.I close: Chytraeus — Luther at Marburg 1529 refused Zwinglians as brothers; Landgrave still sought peace — stop before §.II
pass_a_gloss: The Cause and Author of the Posterior Priority even the Lutheran David Chytraeus himself records, when in his acts with the Zwinglians, in the Marburg colloquy held among Protestants in the year 1529 and fully recited by him, he at last adds: After therefore in the Marburg colloquy Dr. Luther was unwilling to acknowledge and receive as brothers Zwingli, Oecolampadius, Bucer and their associates, because on the article of the true and essential presence of the body and blood of Christ in the Lord’s Supper they taught differently from his opinion, nevertheless the Landgrave and other good men eager for peace and concord did not cease to labor that that dissent on the Lord’s Supper might be piously composed and softened and Christian peace and fraternity established between both parties. p. to me 647.
pass_b_english: Even the Lutheran David Chytraeus records the cause and author of the second priority.

In his full account of the 1529 Marburg colloquy he adds: after Luther refused to acknowledge Zwingli, Oecolampadius, Bucer and their associates as brothers — because they taught differently on the true and essential presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Supper —
the Landgrave and other peace-seekers still did not stop laboring that the Supper dissent might be piously softened and Christian peace and fraternity set between both sides (p. mihi 647).
Stop before §. II (first controversy: interpretation of the Institution words Hoc est corpus meum — literal/κατὰ τὸ ῥητόν vs proper/improper).
source_text: Posterioris Prioritatis Causam Autoremque Lutherum vel ipse Lutheranus Dav. Chytraeus memorat, quando in actis suis cum Zwinglianis, colloquio Marpurgensi inter Protestantes, anno 1529. habito & à se plenè recitato tandem subjicit: Postquam igitur in colloquio Marpurgensi D. Lutherus, Zwinglium, Oecolampadium, Bucerum & eorum socios propterea quod in articulo de vera & essentiali praesentia corporis & sanguinis Christi in Coena Domini, diversum à sententia sua docerent, pro fratribus agnoscere & recipere noluit, Landgravius tamen & alii boni & pacis ac concordiae cupidi non destiterunt in eo elaborare, ut dissensio illa de Coena Domini piè componi & leniri & Christiana pax & fraternitas inter utramque partem constitui posset. p. mihi 647.
